title: Fourth-Order Affine Replacement Bound
statement: Let $(\Omega,\mu)$ be a probability space, and let $A,D,U,V\colon\Omega\to\mathbb R$. Suppose $A,D\in L^4(\mu)$, and suppose each of $U,V$ has mean zero, second moment one, third moment zero, and fourth moment at most $9$ (in particular, each is measurable up to null sets with finite fourth absolute moment). Assume each of $U,V$ is independent of $(A,D)$. Let $\psi\in C^4(\mathbb R)$, and suppose $C\ge0$ bounds $|\psi^{(4)}(t)|$ for every $t\in\mathbb R$. If $\psi(A+DU)$ and $\psi(A+DV)$ are integrable, then $\left|\mathbb E\psi(A+DU)-\mathbb E\psi(A+DV)\right|\le (3C/4)\mathbb E[D^4]$.
hypotheses_covered: $U$ satisfies the fourth-order invariance moment conditions under $\mu$
$V$ satisfies the fourth-order invariance moment conditions under $\mu$
replaced: Let $A,D,U,V$ be real random variables on a probability space, with $A,D\in L^4$. Suppose each of $U,V$ is independent of the pair $(A,D)$ and is measurable up to a null set with finite fourth absolute moment, first three moments $0,1,0$, and fourth moment at most $9$. If $\psi\in C^4(\mathbb R)$, $C\ge0$ bounds $|\psi^{(4)}|$ everywhere, and both $\psi(A+DU)$ and $\psi(A+DV)$ are integrable, then $|\mathbb E\psi(A+DU)-\mathbb E\psi(A+DV)|\le(3C/4)\mathbb E[D^4]$.
